edits.how:
1. Ceiling first, before any phone is paired: in happy-config add the iOS default data commands (location.get, contacts.search, calendar.events, reminders.list, photos.latest, motion.activity, motion.pedometer) to gateway.nodes.commands.deny, keep the opt-in commands (camera.snap, camera.clip, screen.record, health.summary, contacts.add, calendar.add, reminders.add) out of gateway.nodes.commands.allow, and set gateway.nodes.pluginTools.enabled: false so a paired phone cannot publish tools to agents. Deny always wins and both lists are Gateway-wide, so this can ride in the same config change as MAC-04. The deny list matches exact command names, so unless Talk (VOX-01) is being set up also list talk.ptt.start, talk.ptt.stop, talk.ptt.cancel and talk.ptt.once. 2. Install the App Store app on Tony's iPhone and pair it with a setup code from the Control UI (Devices, Pair device) or openclaw qr over the existing Tailscale Serve URL. One code issues a node session and an operator session together; an administrator-minted code approves the device and its first declared command surface in one step, so read the approved command list afterwards and approve any later widening by hand. 3. Access level: Full access carries operator.admin, which is what lets the app review pending exec approvals in general; Limited access drops only operator.admin (write, read and approvals scopes remain) and the docs then promise approval review only for requests that explicitly target that device. 4. Agents: do not grant the built-in nodes tool to any agent (it is owner-only, on the sandbox default deny list, and carries approve and raw invoke actions); if a later feature needs one phone command, use a small in-house plugin tool over api.runtime.nodes.invoke with the node id and command fixed in code. Deny show_widget on

-main, or allow native reports only. 5. Uploads from the app go through the F084 privacy gate, or are switched off with gateway.uploads.enabled: false. iMessage stays the main channel; the app is the surface for long documents, tap approvals and a fallback if imsg breaks after a macOS update. Not planned: a second adult's phone. Every setup code carries Gateway-wide operator scopes, OpenClaw says those are not isolation between people, and roadmap section 1b keeps the control plane with Tony while family members only chat.
